Make a chapter's chunk labels unique across the whole book

Source: R/LandR-related.R
namespaceChunkLabels.Rd

bookdown merges every chapter into one file before knitting, so chunk labels have to be unique across the book and not merely within a module. The modules are written and released separately, and several still carry the labels the SpaDES.core template supplies, so two of them in one book collide and the render stops at knitr's Duplicate chunk label. That is what fireSense_burn and fireSense_ELFs did, both holding module usage example.

Usage

namespaceChunkLabels(lines, modName)

Arguments

lines

character vector of lines.

modName

module name, used as the namespace.

Value

lines, with chunk labels and the references to them rewritten.

Details

Each label gains the module's name, which cannot collide because module names are directory names. A label already ending in it is left exactly as it is, down to its spacing: most module labels are namespaced by hand already, and their knitr cache entries and \\@ref() targets are built on the names they chose. Labels duplicated within one module are then numbered apart, since one module's suffix cannot separate them from each other.

\\@ref(fig:label) and \\@ref(tab:label) move with the labels. bookdown builds a figure's anchor from its chunk label, and addLabel() writes a table's anchor from opts_current$get("label"), so a renamed label whose references stayed behind renders as ?? rather than failing – Biomass_core alone has 19 such references.

An unlabelled chunk is left to knitr, which numbers those across the merged book and so cannot produce a collision.
